clusters.name: After grandfather's death, 1988–1990
clusters.reason: Your mother's anxiety rose over money around 1988, and within months she and your father stopped talking about it. Your grandfather died in July 1989. Around the same time, your brother's grades fell. Your mother's anxiety came back down once she returned to work in early 1990. Three shifts piled up close together around this loss.

clusters.name: After your mother's cancer diagnosis, 1994–1996
clusters.reason: You left for college in September 1993. Six months later you developed migraines that kept you in bed, and you began calling your brother most nights. Your mother was told she had breast cancer in February 1995. Within months you stopped returning your brother's calls and then stopped calling home. Four shifts that count fell between your leaving and your distance from home, around the time your mother's diagnosis became real.
clusters.change: You said the period opened when you left home, but the cancer diagnosis in February 1995 marks the shift in the family that held these events together: your migraines, your reaching toward your brother, then your pulling away from both him and your mother, all clustered around her threatened loss.
